next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: Now that modular_engine is the canonical engine package, integrate it directly with the AtlasForge Dashboard (dashboard_v2.py). Currently the dashboard may reference engine state through indirect paths or legacy APIs. This mission should: (1) Audit dashboard_v2.py for any engine state queries that could be served more cleanly through modular_engine's MissionManager or ExecutionEngine APIs, (2) Add a live engine status endpoint to the dashboard that reads from modular_engine directly, (3) Expose SnapshotManager's state through the /api/recovery/check endpoint so the UI recovery modal has accurate data, (4) Add a modular_engine health check to the dashboard's startup sequence, (5) Write integration tests that confirm dashboard endpoints return correct data from the live modular_engine. The goal is to make dashboard_v2.py a clean consumer of modular_engine's public API, eliminating any remaining indirect state access patterns.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The modular_engine package is now clean and well-structured. The natural next step is to make the dashboard a first-class consumer of its APIs, completing the architectural vision of a modular, observable AtlasForge system. This would complete the separation of concerns: modular_engine owns state, dashboard_v2 observes it through clean APIs.

final_report.summary: Successfully retired the monolithic af_engine.py and replaced it with a structured modular_engine package. The 2-cycle mission decomposed the legacy AtlasForge engine into four focused modules: MissionManager (mission lifecycle), ExecutionEngine (task execution), SnapshotManager (state persistence), and ToolRegistry (tool dispatch). All import sites were migrated from af_engine to modular_engine, af_engine.py was deleted, and the conductor was updated and verified working.
key_achievements: Created modular_engine package with 4 focused modules replacing monolithic af_engine.py
MissionManager: 16,533 bytes of mission lifecycle logic extracted and refactored
ExecutionEngine: 15,937 bytes of task execution logic isolated into its own module
SnapshotManager: 9,498 bytes of state persistence logic in dedicated module
ToolRegistry: 8,282 bytes of tool dispatch logic properly separated

challenges_overcome: Identifying all method calls and attribute accesses on AtlasForgeEngine across atlasforge_conductor.py

lessons_learned: Monolith decomposition works best when done module-by-module with clear domain boundaries
Always verify imports work end-to-end before deleting the legacy file
A single comment documenting the migration is acceptable - not all af_engine references need removal
The modular_engine package structure (core modules + __init__.py facade) is a clean pattern for AtlasForge engine work
Two cycles was the right budget: cycle 1 created the package, cycle 2 completed migration and cleanup
